column1: # What each package installs, once, for every packaging format.
# **This file decides and the built package reports.** Three package
# definitions describing the same software in three dialects is three chances
# to forget a file, and a package missing `esper-engine` installs cleanly and
# does nothing. So the definitions are written in the idiom a packager for that
# distribution expects to read, and `scripts/check-packages.sh` builds them and
# compares what came out against this.
# Paths are not written here because they are not the same on every
# distribution — a licence goes to `/usr/share/licenses` on Arch and
# `/usr/share/doc/<pkg>/copyright` on Debian. What is written here is the
# *kind* of thing, and the checker holds the one mapping from kind to path.
#   bin          an executable                → /usr/bin/<name>
#   unit-user    a systemd user service       → /usr/lib/systemd/user/<name>
#   unit-system  a systemd system service     → /usr/lib/systemd/system/<name>
#   licence      the licence text             → wherever the distribution puts it
